# Let me try clicking on just ONE green block from the top row and see what happens
# The top row green blocks are at row 27, columns 15, 21, 27, 33, 39, 45, 51
result = action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 27, 'col': 15}])
print(f"State: {result.get('state')}")
print(f"Level completed: {result.get('level_completed')}")
print(f"Game over: {result.get('game_over')}")

seg = current_frame.segmentation
greens = [n for n in seg['nodes'] if n['color'] == 'N']
print(f"Green blocks remaining: {len(greens)}")

# Check player position
player = [n for n in seg['nodes'] if n['color'] == 'b']
if player:
    p = player[0]
    center_r = sum(pt[0] for pt in p['boundary']) // len(p['boundary'])
    center_c = sum(pt[1] for pt in p['boundary']) // len(p['boundary'])
    print(f"Player at ({center_r}, {center_c})")

# Check blue regions
blue = [n for n in seg['nodes'] if n['color'] == 'S' and n['pixels'] > 100]
for b in blue:
    center_r = sum(pt[0] for pt in b['boundary']) // len(b['boundary'])
    center_c = sum(pt[1] for pt in b['boundary']) // len(b['boundary'])
    print(f"Blue region at ({center_r}, {center_c}) with {b['pixels']} cells")
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
